title: KV-cache corruption + progressive tenant QoS degradation chaos harness
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description:
Objective: Validate end-to-end system behavior when faced with a compound failure: partial regional partition + intentional KV cache corruption + targeted GPU pool exhaustion for a subset of tenants, while exercising circuit breakers and tenant-priority load-shedding. We want to ensure SLOs degrade predictably, higher-priority tenants keep usable latencies where feasible, circuit breakers open and close as configured, and failover routing does not cascade overload into healthy regions.

Scope: staging and small-production canary only. Test covers: (1) regional routing and failover, (2) prefix/KV cache mismatches that surface stale/inconsistent token streams, (3) simulated GPU pool starvation for a tenant cohort, (4) upstream dependency blackhole (auth service) for a dependent microservice, (5) load-shedding and circuit-breaker interactions with tenant-priority policies.

Hypotheses: 1) Circuit breakers should trip at configured error/latency thresholds and route traffic to fallback model variants without causing mass retries. 2) KV cache corruption (stale prefixes) should be detected by degraded-quality alarms (increase in decoding retries or anomalous token distributions) and trigger automatic eviction of corrupted prefixes. 3) Tenant-priority load-shedding should preserve p95/p99 for high-tier tenants while gracefully returning 429s to low-tier tenants. 4) Multi-region failover must not overload remaining regions beyond safe limits; autoscaling and admission control should hold.

Test plan (ordered):
- Prep: snapshot current canary config, create traffic-shaping job to replay representative traces (control-plane and user requests), enable verbose tracing for token-level metrics, and prepare kill-switch runbook.
- Phase A (Staging): Inject KV prefix mismatch into staging inference runtime for a single model shard (simulate off-by-one key index). Observe error patterns and quality regressions.
- Phase B (Staging): Introduce a dependency blackhole for the auth service in staging for 10 minutes while monitoring circuit-breaker and fallback flows.
- Phase C (Small prod canary, controlled tenants ~5%): Orchestrate a soft region partition (announce / route a subset of control-plane traffic away from region-us-east-2) while simultaneously throttling 60% of GPU allocation in that region to simulate pool starvation for tenant cohort T1.
- Phase D (Canary): Enable tenant-priority shedding rules (high/medium/low) and measure distribution of 200/429/503 responses, latency percentiles, and token-level cost delta.
- Abort/Recover: At any sign of cross-region overload or SLO shock (see rollback criteria), execute immediate rollback via routing policy revert and GPU pool reallocation.

Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency per-tenant, error-rate (5xx + retries), token output quality signals (BLEU-like or custom eval hooks), number of circuit-breaker opens per minute, fallback invocation rate, admission control reject rate, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit/miss/eviction counts, and control-plane loopback latency.

Runbook & Safety controls:
- Preflight checklist: Run synthetic smoke tests, ensure canary tenants are notified, confirm run hours window and pager coverage, check autoscaler headroom >= 20% across target regions.
- Kill-switch: one-click routing rollback (console -> routing -> revert to baseline) plus infra playbooks to reassign GPU capacity.
- Guardrails: max injected duration 10 minutes for each sub-fault, auto-abort if global 5xx > 1% sustained for 3 minutes or if p99 for high-tier exceeds baseline by 3x.

Acceptance criteria:
- Circuit breakers open within expected threshold and fallback models are invoked for >= 95% of failing calls.
- High-tier tenant p99 latency increases by <= 2x baseline during canary.
- Low-tier tenants see >= 60% of requests rejected (429) under shedding policy when under severe GPU starvation.
- No region experiences sustained overload beyond 85% GPU utilization after failover routing.
- Annotated metrics and logs uploaded to the dashboard with at least three correlated traces showing end-to-end failover + recovery.
